🎙
Opening remarks
by Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at the ninth Russia-Gulf Cooperation Council (
#GCC
) Joint Ministerial Meeting for Strategic Dialogue
(Manama, October 18, 2026)
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
First of all, I would like to congratulate you on
the 45th anniversary of the establishment of the GCC
, which we mark in 2026.
Strengthening multifaceted, mutually beneficial ties with the GCC member states is
among the priorities of Russia’s foreign policy and diplomacy
.
The Strategic Dialogue with the Arab states of the Gulf was established
almost 15 years ago
in Abu Dhabi. Year after year, it has demonstrated its continued relevance and effectiveness, enabling f
rank and constructive exchanges on the most delicate global and regional issues
and
helping us map out further practical steps
to expand trade, economic, cultural and humanitarian ties between our countries.
☝️
The importance of such direct engagement can hardly be overstated amid a rapidly changing geopolitical landscape.
Russia and all GCC Member States
maintain regular, active contacts at the highest level
, giving powerful impetus to the comprehensive development of our relations.
We have established close foreign policy coordination
. I value the frank and trusting personal dialogue I enjoy with each of you, dear friends. I warmly recall our productive discussion during the previous,
eighth round of the Strategic Dialogue in Sochi in September 2025
.
📈
In 2025, Russia’s total trade with the GCC Member States grew by 45%
. Since 2021, almost every country in the Council has been a guest of honour at one of Russia’s major annual events,
the St Petersburg International Economic Forum
. We welcome this tradition and would like to see it continue.
The effectiveness of our economic cooperation depends to a considerable extent on
regional stability
. I look forward to discussing the Middle East’s most pressing problems in detail today, above all the situation in and around the Gulf.
The region remains gripped by a serious military and political crisis
that erupted following
the unprovoked US and Israeli aggression against Iran
, triggering a chain reaction across many other flashpoints in the Middle East.
❗️
Russia supports efforts to promote peace,
including those undertaken by the countries represented here
, aimed at preventing a return to full-scale war in the region.
We see
our updated Concept of Collective Security in the Persian Gulf
as our contribution to these efforts
. You are familiar with it. Earlier versions of this document have been discussed for decades with representatives of political, academic and expert circles in the GCC countries.
We believe that
the Gulf’s littoral states themselves must have the decisive say in determining how to ensure the secure development
of this entire, vitally important region.
Our Concept
is aimed precisely at creating conditions for direct dialogue among the Gulf’s littoral states and their neighbours, such as Iraq and Jordan.
🤝
Let me stress that
we sincerely cherish our friendly relations with all GCC members
and
remain firmly committed to steadily advancing our Strategic Dialogue
for the benefit of our countries and peoples.

item.title: 🇷🇺 On October 18, Foreign Minister of Russia Sergey Lavrov and Foreign Minister of Saudi Arabia Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇸🇦 On October 18, Foreign Minister of Russia Sergey Lavrov and Foreign Minister of Saudi Arabia Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud held a meeting in Manama on the sidelines of the ninth Ministerial Meeting of the Russia-Gulf Cooperation Council ( #GCC ) Strategic Dialogue . The Ministers discussed priority issues in the multifaceted Russia-Saudi Arabia relationship. Both Sides expressed their commitment to maintaining regular, frank political dialogue and expanding trade, economic, investment, cultural and humanitarian cooperation . They reaffirmed the importance of continuing effective cooperation between Russia and Saudi Arabia within the #OPECplus framework. The Ministers considered current international and Middle Eastern issues , including the situation in the Persian Gulf. They expressed concern over tensions in the southern Arabian Peninsula and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Both Sides emphasised the importance of ensuring the safety of navigation and the unimpeded passage of vessels through all international waterways. #RussiaSaudiArabia

item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://t.me/MFARussia/32806

🎙
Statement
by Deputy Head of the Delegation of the Russian Federation, Deputy Director of the Department for Non-Proliferation and Arms Control of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation Konstantin Vorontsov at the Thematic Debate on Cluster I “Nuclear Weapons” in the First Committee of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly
📍
New York, October 16, 2026
💬
Russia is committed to the ideals of nuclear disarmament according to a comprehensive approach envisaged by
the provisions of the NPT
. The Treaty unconditionally remains for us
the key legal benchmark and the foundation for the efforts
in this field. <...>
We consider ideas of a “shortcut” to “nuclear zero” – providing for the immediate and unconditional renunciation of nuclear weapons through arbitrarily outlawing them –
to be unrealistic and counterproductive
.
We are firmly convinced that disarmament initiatives must be appropriate for the military-political and strategic context.
The nuclear disarmament process, in particular, cannot be separated from the state of affairs in relations between nuclear-weapon States.
<...>
❌
Factors
which have
an extremely negative impact on the military-political and strategic situation
, and thereby hinder the implementation of disarmament initiatives, include, amongst others:
• NATO’s
self-proclaimed “nuclear status”
and the development by the bloc of schemes and means of “nuclear sharing” based on the forward deployment of the US nuclear weapons;
• the inclusion of elements of the NATO nuclear sharing into
the United States “extended deterrence” arrangements
in the Asia-Pacific region
, with a tendency towards establishing a tripartite “nuclear alliance” between the United States, the Republic of Korea and Japan;
• the shift by the European nuclear-weapon States towards
building up their arsenals
, joint planning for their use, and engaging non-nuclear NATO allies in a multifaceted support for such operations within the framework of “forward deterrence” and other algorithms complementing the US nuclear “umbrella”;
• the establishment of
a global and multi-domain US missile defence system
coupled with the build-up of offensive systems designed for a disarming first strike;
• the forward
deployment of the United States-made and other Western-made ground-launched intermediate-range and shorter-range missiles
;
•
US steps to deploy weapons in outer space
;
• the NATO countries’ pursuit of consolidation of their cumulative advantage in non-nuclear military capabilities in all operational environments;
• bringing the NATO strategic military infrastructure
close to the borders of Russia
and its allies, accompanied by a destabilising build-up of significant combat forces in those areas.
***
The
NPT
remains one of the cornerstones of international peace and security.
<...>
It is important
to exclude the use of the NPT and non-proliferation rhetoric for pursuing narrow, selfish political objectives
unrelated to the Treaty’s objectives, let alone for justifying military aggression against undesired countries.
The mechanism for verifying States’ compliance with their non-proliferation obligations, and
the
IAEA
safeguards system as its core element, should not be undermined
. <...>
This year marks
the 30th anniversary of the opening for signature of
the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty
(
#CTBT
).
The Russian Federation
was the first
of the five nuclear-weapon States to join the CTBT and did so on the day it was opened for signature, September 24, 1996. Russia remains a State Signatory to the CTBT, with all the rights and obligations arising from that status.
❗️
However, if the United States or other States Parties to the Treaty conduct full-scale nuclear tests, Russia, too, will have to appropriately and adequately respond. We continue to follow this approach consistently.

item.description: 🗓 On October 15, the Fourth Committee of the UN General Assembly adopted a resolution entitled “Addressing Contemporary Forms of Colonialism” . The draft was prepared by the Group of Friends in Defence of the UN Charter , with Russia’s active participation. 19 states co-sponsored the resolution . 🌐 The resolution is non-confrontational and unifying in nature. It stresses the need to eradicate neocolonial practices , including interference in internal affairs, unilateral coercive measures, the imposition of unfair international treaties and restrictions on technological development. On October 15,
the Fourth Committee
of the UN General Assembly
adopted
a resolution entitled
“Addressing Contemporary Forms of Colonialism”
.
The draft was prepared by
the Group of Friends in Defence of the UN Charter
, with Russia’s active participation.
19 states co-sponsored the resolution
.
🌐
The resolution is non-confrontational and unifying in nature.
It stresses the need to eradicate neocolonial practices
, including interference in internal affairs, unilateral coercive measures, the imposition of unfair international treaties and restrictions on technological development.
These practices are among
the most serious obstacles to achieving the purposes and principles of
the UN Charter
and are a root cause of numerous problems on the UN agenda.
✅
The document was supported by 85 Member States,
with 49 voting against and 23 abstaining.
Significantly, its supporters included
#BRICS
countries
and states across
Africa
,
Asia
and
Latin America
, while its opponents were predominantly countries of the “collective West”, many of them
former colonial powers
. The latter refused to support the document, despite having participated in drafting it and having some of their amendments incorporated into the final text.
The voting results clearly demonstrate that the emergence of a
#MultipolarWorld
is well underway
. Freeing interstate relations from all forms of pressure, subordination and dependence is an integral part of this process.
The Global Majority is unwilling to accept the monopoly held by a small group of countries.
For these states, combating neocolonialism is no abstract notion: it is a matter of pursuing sovereign domestic and foreign policies, strengthening their security and preserving their national identity.
☝️
We expect the adopted resolution
, which builds on two previous thematic resolutions of the General Assembly,
to gain even broader support when it is considered shortly at a plenary meeting of the
#UNGA
.
This will help firmly establish
the fight against all manifestations of colonialism
as one of the UN key priorities.

item.title: 🇷🇺 On October 16, President of Russia Vladimir Putin and Pope Leo XIV had a telephone conversation
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇻🇦 📞 On October 16, President of Russia Vladimir Putin and Pope Leo XIV had a telephone conversation . After wishing the supreme pontiff sound health and a speedy recovery after the surgery he had undergone recently, Vladimir Putin emphasised the importance of the cooperation between Russia and the Vatican in promoting common moral values and protecting Christians and Christian shrines across the world . Both Sides reaffirmed their interest in maintaining dialogue between the Russian Orthodox Church and the Catholic Church. During an exchange of views on the situation surrounding Ukraine, Vladimir Putin thanked the Pope for his willingness to contribute to resolving the conflict and his humanitarian efforts . In response to the Pontiff’s concern for civilians in the Russian city of Alyoshki , Kherson Region, comprehensive explanations were provided regarding the Kiev regime’s responsibility for the difficult humanitarian situation there. Support was expressed for the Vatican’s intention to help create conditions to ensure the safety of the city’s population and arrange deliveries of vital supplies. It was agreed to cooperate on this matter. Support was expressed for the Vatican's intention to facilitate creating the necessary conditions to keep the town's population safe and beginning vital supplies . The two Sides agreed to cooperate in this regard. The conversation was constructive and mutually respectful.

item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://t.me/MFARussia/32802

🎙
Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman
Maria Zakharova
’s
answer to a media question
regarding
Poland’s plans concerning the Kaliningrad Region
(October 16, 2026)
❓
Question: In a recent interview with the Italian newspaper La Repubblica, Chair of the NATO Military Committee Admiral Giuseppe Cavo Dragone said that the North Atlantic Alliance had no plans to blockade Kaliningrad. “I want to be absolutely clear: NATO is not preparing any blockade of Kaliningrad. This is a threat built around a scenario that does not exist,” he emphasised. How would you comment on this?
Maria Zakharova:
Yes, such a statement was indeed made. Let us assume, difficult as it may be to believe, that the Admiral is being sincere this time. If so, what plans are actually being drawn up?
For example, on October 12, at the annual Warsaw Security Forum, one of the central events was a keynote address by NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe General Alexus Grynkewich, entitled Theory of Victory: How Do We Achieve Military Success Against Russia in Deterrence and Defence?
A senior NATO general chose Warsaw, t
he capital of a country currently pursuing militarisation at a breakneck pace
, to present his proposals, the analytical merits of which we shall leave you to judge. It is worth noting that Poland harbours ambitions to turn its Wojsko Polskie into perhaps the most powerful military in Europe, and specific scenarios for its deployment are already being drawn up.
For instance, the General Staff of the Polish Armed Forces has developed operational plans for launching
pre-emptive precision strikes against the Kaliningrad Region
, should a “war with Russia become inevitable”. Just consider this: nothing has happened yet, but the Polish hussars are already charging ahead in formation.
Specifically, the plan envisages the destruction of all military infrastructure, primarily Iskander and S-400 missile systems, as well as ammunition depots, fuel terminals and command posts. The operation would involve US-made HIMARS and Polish Homar-K missile systems with a range of up to 300 kilometres, F-16 fighter jets armed with precision-guided missiles with a range of up to 1,000 kilometres, loitering munitions and combat UAVs.
At the same time, Polish coastal anti-ship missile systems and NATO aircraft would be used to i
mpose a naval blockade on the Kaliningrad Region
. The aim would be to prevent Baltic Fleet vessels from leaving their bases and to cut off the region’s supply routes. In parallel, a ground offensive in the Suwałki Gap is envisaged, involving the 16th and 18th Mechanised Divisions and the 1st Infantry Division of the Polish Armed Forces.
Is this not essentially Operation Barbarossa 2.0?
❗️
However, the “strategists” in Warsaw and elsewhere would do well to remember what President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
and Foreign Minister
Sergey Lavrov
have
repeatedly stated
:
any treacherous armed attack against the Kaliningrad Region
will be met with a literally incinerating response
, using every means at Russia’s disposal.
The war will be very short.
